text:
maya: quick proposal — we should move from pure env-based TTLs to a hybrid rule set: base TTL by env (prod:30d, stage:14d, dev:3d) + promotion rules for error/failure traces and for sampled high-latency flows. keeps hot storage for important spans without blowing cost. thoughts?

sam: sounds reasonable. can you sketch how promotion rules would work? e.g., if an error span appears, do we promote the whole trace or just the span?

maya: promote full trace for now — we need context for debugging. promotion window = 7d (i.e., when promoted it gets 7d hot retention on top of base). also add auto-demote if no errors in X days.

liam: concerns about bursty errors during deploys — we could end up promoting a ton. maybe add rate-limit and top-N per service per minute. also consider a severity threshold (error vs warn).

maya: agree on rate-limiting. proposed rule:
```
- base_ttl: { prod: 30d, stage: 14d, dev: 3d }
- promote_if: span.status == "error" || span.latency > p99_service_latency
- promote_limit: 200 traces/service/minute
- promotion_ttl: 7d
- demote_if: no error events in 14d
```

nora: how does this interact with exporters and sampling? e.g., otel exporters often sample before exporting which could lose the trace we want to promote.

maya: right — two parts: 1) low-level sampling for cost, 2) dynamic tail-sampling at collector to force-export interesting traces. collector should have short memory to decide on promotion and flush. we need a path to request re-ingest for promoted traces if sampling dropped them.

sam: asking for re-ingest sounds hard. maybe we do capture a small dag of metadata (trace id, service, error flag) even for sampled-out traces so collector can pull full spans from local buffers when promotion triggers?

liam: we already keep a tiny LRU buffer in the agent for 5s of recent spans. enlarge to 30s for safety and add a callback to flush on promotion. cost is marginal.

nora: add a note for compliance: promoted traces may contain PII; ensure KMS tagging and audit log for any promotion action. ops-bot can enforce masking rules before hot-tier writes.

ops-bot: reminder — current hot-tier capacity is 200GB/day growth sustainable. estimated promotion rate at 2% of prod traces would exceed that. please include cost projection in the RFC. :warning:

maya: good catch. i'll run projection with a few scenarios (0.5%, 1%, 2%) and include autoscaling / archive fallback. also adding threshold-based permanent cold fallback if budget exceeded.

sam: UX question for console — we should surface which rules caused a trace to be promoted in the trace header (e.g., "promoted_by: error-rule-1") so support sees why it's hot.

maya: yes — plan to add metadata labels: promoted_by, promotion_ts, original_sample_rate. console will add a filter for promoted traces.

liam: one more — alerting. If promotions spike suddenly, trigger an ops paging policy so we don't hit capacity silently.

nora: ok next steps: maya to PR RFC with example rules + cost table, liam to prototype expanded agent buffer + flush hook, sam to draft console metadata UX, i'll check compliance details. deadline EOD Friday?

maya: EOD Friday works. i'll drop a link to the RFC when ready. :+1:
